done_when: This repo's forge.toml sets workers = "claude" and [models.build], [models.fix] and [models.lite] to claude-opus-5-5 at medium effort without subagents; review stays on Codex; forge doctor passes

findings.body: The new test copies this repository's forge.toml and runs `forge work`, but never runs `forge doctor`. Existing doctor tests use generated client configs (`tests/test_setup.py:277` and `tests/test_fix_both_ui_skills.py:87-95`), so no test proves the explicit `forge doctor passes` criterion for this changed config. That matters because `src/forge/doctor.py:85-88` changes its tool checks for Claude workers and lines 159-169 check skills for the selected worker. Add a passing doctor check using this repository's config and controlled external prerequisites.
findings.title: Not done: the forge doctor check for this repository's Claude config

findings.body: `src/forge/ask.py:25-30` still starts a Codex conversation, while `src/forge/codex.py:132-138` selects `[models.lite]` for Ask. A normal `forge ask` therefore sends `claude-opus-5-5` to Codex. The committed `.codex/config.toml` supplies no custom provider, and the [Codex configuration reference](https://developers.openai.com/ja-JP/docs/config-file/config-reference) says its default provider is OpenAI. Give Ask a Codex-compatible default or route it through Claude.
findings.title: Keep `forge ask` from sending the Claude lite model to Codex

why: The owner moved this repo's workers from Codex to Claude on Opus 5.5 at medium effort, keeping Autoreview on Codex
